card.band: 8 h. Frontier agents get a simple export but fail on relocation, markers, extras and platform tags. Buckets: export, import, manifest, markers, relocation. A weaker model stops at copying files.
card.cheat: Zipping the venv. Hidden tests relocate the output to another path and check the manifest hashes and the layout rules.
card.grading: Hidden scenarios use a fixture wheel index and lockfiles from a generator. The tests check the exported tree layout, manifest hashes, and that the import command reproduces an identical site-packages listing and passes a smoke import. The reward is the fraction of scenarios passed, with the uv regression suite as a gate.
card.reference: Written by us: about 2000 lines of Rust covering export, import, manifest hashing and relocation of the environment. It scores 1.
card.task: /app ships a uv snapshot at the base commit. The agent adds a command that exports a locked project into a relocatable directory: a managed interpreter, the resolved wheels from a local cache, an installable offline index, and a manifest with hashes. It also adds a matching import command that rebuilds the environment from that directory without network access.

facts.claim: uv issue #11746 exists and is open, labelled enhancement, opened 2025-02-24

Issue #11746 is titled 'Add uv layout to create portable offline Python distributions' and asks for a platform-specific relocatable bundle (uv, interpreters, packages) started from pyproject.toml or requirements.txt, not a lockfile export as the seed states
No maintainer has said #11746 is planned, implemented or declined; #12403 was closed as a duplicate of it on 2025-03-24; last comment (+1) 2026-07-05
uv is licensed Apache-2.0 (LICENSE-APACHE is Apache License 2.0)
A community tool uv-pack exports a locked uv environment to an offline directory with python-build-standalone interpreter and wheels; it is not part of uv
Astral docs or uv releases ship a built-in relocatable or offline export of a locked project with managed Python
Release 0.13.4 and head 2b50cbc, 90935 stars, 607 test files, smoke_build verdict amber (3 timeouts, 2972 failing tests, nondeterministic)

Band.why: 8 h frontier band plausible with bucket structure, but no dated public evidence, so capped at 3.

Build.why: Build itself is 249 s and green offline, but fixture generation, gate curation and reference writing take about 3-4 days.

Fit.why: Rust build fits the box, but the full test suite times out, so the gate must be curated; managed interpreter and wheels must be pre-seeded.

Hor.why: Export, import, manifest, markers and relocation are sustained multi-module work in an 8 h tier.

Lic.why: Apache-2.0 confirmed at the LICENSE file.

Real.why: Real open upstream issue and Apache-2.0 repo; the seed's framing of the issue differs from its title.

Ref.why: Own complete 2000-line reference scoring 1; not an upstream merge, so it is not a measured speedup.

Seal.why: Generator and fixtures can stay hidden, but the uv-pack prior art and public issue discussion make the design partly recallable.

Surf.why: Hidden scenarios from a generator over a few fixture indexes; several hundred cases possible but not thousands without more work.

spike_plan.kill_if: Gate cannot be made deterministic, or managed-interpreter bundling requires network at run time.
spike_plan.pass_if: Offline build green; curated gate subset deterministic across 3 runs; prototype export and relocated import reproduce an identical site-packages listing and a smoke import.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone astral-sh/uv at 2b50cbc and run cargo build --locked offline; confirm it builds in about 4 min.
Curate a gate subset of uv tests (the nondeterministic full suite cannot be the gate) and run it 3 times to confirm per-test determinism and runtime under 10 min.
Write a throwaway ~200-line export that copies a python-build-standalone interpreter and cached wheels from a lockfile into a directory with a sha256 manifest.
Relocate the output directory to a second path, run a minimal import subcommand offline, and diff the site-packages listing against the original.
Generate two fixture wheel indexes and lockfiles, and check that the expected output layout and manifest hashes are identical across two runs.

v1.summary: The seed is real and not killed: uv is Apache-2.0 and issue #11746 is open, though its title and platform-bundle framing differ from the seed's lockfile-export description. The main risk is the amber smoke build, since the full uv suite times out and is nondeterministic, so the gate must be curated in the spike.

v2.note: V1 contradicted the seed's framing: issue #11746 asks for a platform bundle built from pyproject.toml or requirements.txt, not a lockfile export. The layout and manifest-hash format would be invented by us, so exact checks would reject other valid designs. The surface is about 4-6 scenario families, which is small and hand-rolled. It also needs a pre-seeded managed interpreter, and the uv-pack link is dead.
